title: File state annual report
summary: File the annual report and keep the company in good standing with your state of incorporation. The ritual differs by state: California's Statement of Information is due within 90 days of registration and annually after (law rule us-ca.statement-of-information), Nevada's annual list lands by the end of the anniversary month alongside the $500 business-license renewal (law rule us-nv.annual-list-business-license), and Texas ties standing to the May 15 franchise tax report (law rule us-tx.franchise-tax-report).

parts.title: Gather filing details
parts.guidance: Identify the state report, entity type and period from the official record and current instructions. Compare requested addresses, officers or managers and agent details with the company’s records, resolving changes before certification. Keep private information in the filing workspace. Separate this report from any franchise-tax, income-tax or licensing work so the correct task is prepared.

parts.title: File the annual report on the state portal
parts.guidance: Select the correct entity, report and period in the official portal. Compare prefilled information with current company records and identify changes requiring a separate filing. The authorized filer reviews the declaration and approves submission and fees. Preserve the submitted report and check whether it was accepted or needs correction.

verify.how: The state portal shows the report filed and the entity in good standing for the year.

parts.title: Save the confirmation receipt
parts.guidance: Save the submitted report, payment receipt and acceptance evidence under the correct entity and period. If review is pending, track that status until resolved. Update the compliance calendar from the state’s actual next requirement and make the files retrievable by the person responsible for the next cycle.

parts.title: File the California Statement of Information (bizfile Online)
parts.guidance: Check the California entity’s Statement of Information obligation and filing period in bizfile Online. Establish the authorized filer’s required access and review the requested company details. Complete submission and fees through the entity’s authorized filing route. Save the filed statement and confirmation, then use this entity’s actual next filing schedule.

parts.title: File the annual report in each registered state
parts.guidance: Review the current report or renewal requirements for every registered state and entity type. Determine what is due, the period covered and who will file it, including states with no report due this cycle. Submit approved filings and preserve their individual acceptance records. Check obligations against the official record when a notice is missing.

parts.title: File the Nevada annual list and renew the state business license
parts.guidance: Nevada corporations file the annual list of officers and directors on or before the last day of the anniversary month of incorporation, with the $500 state business license renewal running alongside it and the list fee scaling with authorized stock (law rule us-nv.annual-list-business-license). File through SilverFlume, the state business portal, and keep the declaration and receipts with the entity's compliance records. Defaulting corporations face revocation and reinstatement costs.

parts.title: File the Texas franchise tax report and Public Information Report
parts.guidance: Texas ties an entity's standing to the annual franchise tax report, due May 15; entities at or below the no-tax-due threshold still file the Public Information Report or Ownership Report (law rule us-tx.franchise-tax-report). File through the Comptroller's Webfile and resolve any forfeiture notices promptly — forfeiture cuts off the right to sue and exposes officers to liability. Keep the filed report with the entity's compliance records.

parts.title: File the New York biennial statement ($9)
parts.guidance: New York corporations file a Biennial Statement with the Department of State every two years under Business Corporation Law § 408, due in the calendar month in which the original Certificate of Incorporation or Application for Authority was filed, with a $9 fee (law rule us-ny.biennial-statement). File through the e-Statement Filing Service using the exact entity name and DOS ID; a missed statement marks the record past due on any certificate of status. The statement cannot be filed before its due month.

cost.note: Biennial Statement filing fee under the Business Corporation Law. Conditional step — excluded from the default-flow fee headline by construction.

parts.title: File the Florida annual report (January 1 – May 1, $150)
parts.guidance: Florida profit corporations file the Sunbiz annual report between January 1 and May 1 each year after the formation or qualification year, with a $150 fee; after May 1 a $400 late fee is assessed with no waiver provision, and an entity still unfiled by the third Friday in September faces administrative dissolution (law rule us-fl.annual-report). File online with the document number on record and confirm the emailed filing confirmation. Reinstatement after dissolution costs $600 plus each missed year's report fee.

cost.note: 'Profit Annual Report (with supplemental fee)'; $550 total when received after May 1. Conditional step — excluded from the default-flow fee headline by construction.

metadata.supportReason: State filing portals have no API — the filing is manual form work; gathering the details and saving the receipt are agent steps.

slugAliases.label: File an annual report / registered agent

geoNotes.summary: The annual-report analog is the MCA annual return (MGT-7/MGT-7A) plus financial statements (AOC-4), due after the AGM each year on MCA V3 (fronted by NSWS — mca.gov.in blocks automated access); late fees accrue per day.
The direct analog is the confirmation statement: at least annually, £34 online, confirming registered details to Companies House — miss it and the registrar can strike the company off.

The ritual here is disclosure: every GmbH must file (or for micro-companies deposit) annual accounts electronically for the Unternehmensregister within 12 months of year-end — enforced with automatic Bundesanzeiger fine proceedings.

The analog is the dépôt des comptes annuels: accounts approved by the shareholders within 6 months of year-end, then filed via the guichet unique to the commercial-court registry (confidentiality options exist for small companies).

The annual keep-in-good-standing filing is the IES: accounts to the registry, tax annexes and statistics in one electronic declaration — miss it and tax-authority fines plus an outdated registry record follow.
File the annual return with Corporations Canada within 60 days of the anniversary date (a corporate-records filing, not a tax return) — corporations that skip it can be administratively dissolved.

The direct analog is the Companies Office annual return: every year in your allocated filing month, $49.74 plus GST, confirming the register information — miss it and the Registrar may remove the company from the register.
geoNotes.actionLabel: Complete your annual return — Companies Register

geoNotes.summary: The direct analog is the ACRA annual return: every company files one each year through Bizfile, within 7 months after the financial year end for non-listed companies — miss it and late penalties and eventual striking off follow.

The direct analog is ASIC's annual statement at the review date: confirm the company's registered details, pay the annual review fee, and have the directors pass the solvency resolution within 2 months of the review date.
No annual report or confirmation statement exists: the corporate registry is event-driven, with changes registered within two weeks of occurring (Commercial Act Article 183).

The annual report (majandusaasta aruanne) goes to the commercial register within six months after the financial year ends (law rule ee.annual-report-deadline), prepared and filed through the e-Business Register.
